node-1.label: Bilateral conjunctival erythema and asymptomatic skin lesions on the lower limbs, trunk, and upper limbs

node-2.label: 65-year-old man with medical history of coronary artery disease, treated dyslipidemia, and hypertension; initial ophthalmology presentation showed bilateral conjunctival erythema and choroidal thickening

node-3.label: One year after initial presentation, asymptomatic skin lesions appeared on lower limbs and progressed to trunk and upper limbs; a 3-week tapered course of oral prednisone (60 mg/d) showed no improvement; physical examination revealed many flat, firm, brownish papules and plaques resembling keloids, some linear with an arborizing pattern, symmetrically involving lower limbs, trunk, and upper limbs while sparing face, oral mucosa, and flexor regions

node-4.label: One year later, immunoglobulin G–κ type monoclonal gammopathy developed
